During the examination-in-chief, you said that Brne at one point in time swore at Mladic, Krajisnik and Karadzic; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: PERICA KOBLAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: Why didn't you say that in any other statement of yours, that he cursed Mladic's, Krajisnik's and Karadzic's mother?

utterances.speaker: PERICA KOBLAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those words were addressed to Zivko Krajisnik, and when he swore at Karadzic and Mladic and Krajisnik, that was in the context of the fact that Zivko Krajisnik couldn't be saved by anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: I'm asking you now, if that is something very vivid, you have a Serb soldier, Serb officer, commander, who at a given point curses the mother of the main commander of the Army of Republika Srpska, the president of Republika Srpska and president of the National Assembly of Republika Srpska, as far as I'm concerned that is something that is lodged in one's memory. But you don't mention that in any of these two statements given to the Muslim authorities or in the statement that you gave in 2004 to The Hague investigators. You mention that cursing and swearing for the first time during yesterday's examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: PERICA KOBLAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be in the first statement after I fled from Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. SESELJ
utterances.text: The cursing of these people's mothers is not mentioned in any of the statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, your time is up. Mr. Ferrara, what were you saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: That is exactly what the witness mentioned in the statement he gave to the ICTY investigator, page 5 of the statement, paragraph 12, where he says that Brne said: "You Serb bastard, no Krajisnik, Karadzic or Mladic will save you now. In fact, Karadzic, Krajisnik and Mladic, they are nothing in Bosnia ..." And so on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is really quite unbelievable. Nowhere in any of the statements does it say that this witness said that Brne swore at Mladic, Krajisnik and Karadzic and cursed their mother. That is the worst type of swear word that you can use in the Serbian language. It's quite another thing to say they could all fuck off, Krajisnik, et cetera. You can say that when you're having a sort of loose exchange with someone, but I'm afraid that this was not properly translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj, we have to stop now because we are five minutes away from the end. On paragraph 12 of the statement, what Brne would have said about Momcilo Krajisnik, Karadzic and Mladic, but you are right to say that nothing is mentioned about the mother. All right, that is --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to tell you one more thing. I'm afraid of this translation in English, and I'd like to know what expression was used in English. If the expression was used that begins with the letter "F," then that certainly doesn't have the same meaning in Serbian and English. In English, that is a swear word, something ugly is mentioned, whereas in Serbian this has become the vernacular. When you say "zajebancija," it means it's a joke, it's just joking around, and in fact in English you can use perhaps a more vulgar term for "joke." But if the word was used that I think was used was actually used, then it has quite a different meaning. The witness did not say that Karadzic's mother was invoked and that the swear word cursed their mothers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You are raising an objection on a potential translation issue, so we shall ask the Translation Department to translate paragraph 12 of this statement, to translate from B/C/S into English. Mr. Ferrara, do you have any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. FERRARA
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to thank you, since you've stayed here for two days. On behalf of the Bench, I would like to wish you a safe journey home, and I wish you all the best in your future endeavours and teaching. I shall ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm now addressing the Prosecution. We don't have time to bring the witness into the courtroom and ask him to take the solemn declaration. He was waiting outside, and we thought that he might be able to come in. So, Mr. Mundis, what about the witness for tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The witness that's currently listed on the schedule, who was to start testifying today, will be available to testify tomorrow, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. Mundis. I believe you've asked to have two and a half hours. With all the objections and interruptions, if you have two and a half hours and Mr. Seselj has two and a half hours, we will need at least two days, which means that the witness will have to stay on until Tuesday. Can you check this with him, to see that he is available?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We will attempt to do so tomorrow morning, immediately prior to the witness testifying. I don't believe he's any longer in the building. We'll endeavor to do that first thing in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. For the time being, we have two and a half hours for the Prosecution and two and a half hours for Mr. Seselj, but experience has shown us that two and a half hours plus two and a half hours equals five hours, but it will be longer than that and the witness will have to stay on until next week. It is now 7.00 and time to adjourn. Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, according to reliable information, that witness can't wait to stay in The Hague the whole weekend, over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All the better. We will have no problems, therefore. It is now 7.00. See you tomorrow. Let me remind you that we shall start our hearing at 9.00 tomorrow morning, so make your arrangements, Mr. Seselj. Make sure you're here at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 12th day of June, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
